name: Correlation Analysis
description: Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation between variables
whenToUse: When two or more numeric variables may be related: computes the correlation of two columns (Pearson, Spearman and Kendall side by side, with confidence interval and diagnostics) or of three or more columns as a correlation matrix; each column needs at least 5 numeric values.
noWorksheet: Add a Worksheet module first to provide data.
noNumericColumns: No numeric columns found in any worksheet.
recNormal: Both variables are approximately normally distributed — Pearson r is optimally applicable.
recNotNormal: At least one variable is not normally distributed — rank-based methods (Spearman/Kendall) are more robust.
recOutliers: {count} outliers detected in residuals — Pearson r is biased. Rank-based methods are more resistant.
recNoOutliers: No outliers detected — Pearson r is not biased by extreme values.
recNonlinear: Pearson r and Spearman ρ differ by Δ = {delta} — indicates non-linear but monotonic relationship.
recLinear: Pearson and Spearman agree well (Δ = {delta}) — linear relationship likely.
recSmallN: Small sample (n = {n}) — Kendall τ has better statistical properties for small n.
recLargeN: Sufficient sample size (n = {n}) — all three methods are statistically reliable.
recLowMono: Monotonicity index low ({pct}%) — relationship may not be monotonic.
errColumnMissing: A chosen column no longer exists. Choose the columns again.

invariants.uniqueColumnRefs: Each column may be chosen only once.
